for, “Who is hearing?”

But you, Yahweh, laugh at them.
You mock all of the nations.

Let me wait for you, his strength,
for God is my stronghold.

The God of my covenant faithfulness will meet me.
God will make me look upon my enemies.

Do not slay them, lest my people forget.
Scatter them by your power and bring them down, Lord, our shield.

For the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips,
may they be taken in their pride,
and for the curse and for the lying they tell.

Consume them in wrath;
consume them that they may not be,
that they may know that God is ruling in Jacob
to the ends of the earth. Selah

They return at evening;
they growl like a dog and go around the city.

They, they wander around to eat.
If they are not full, then they lodge.

But I, I will sing about your strength,
and I will sing aloud in the morning about your covenant faithfulness!
For you are a stronghold to me
and a refuge in the day of trouble to me.

Let me make music to you, my strength,
for God is my stronghold, the God of my covenant faithfulness.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on “The Lily.” A testimony. A miktam of David, for teaching. When he fought with Aram Naharaim and with Aram Zobah, and Joab returned and struck Edom in the Valley of Salt, 12, 000.
verses.text:
God, you have rejected us; you have broken through us.
You have become angry; restore us!

You have made the earth tremble; you have broken it.
Heal its breaches, for it shakes.

You have made your people see the difficult.
You have made us drink the wine of staggering.

You have given a banner to the ones fearing you,
to be displayed from the face of the bow. Selah

So that your beloved may be delivered,
save us with your right hand and answer me.

To me is Gilead, and to me is Manasseh.
And Ephraim is the protection of my head; Judah, my scepter.

Moab is the tub of my washing.
Over Edom I throw my sandal.
Over me, Philistia, shout triumphantly.”

Who will bring me into the city of fortification?
Who will lead me to Edom?

You, God, have you not rejected us?
And you do not go out with our armies, God.

Give help against the enemy to us,
for the salvation of man is futility.

With God we will do valor,
for he, he will trample our adversaries.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on a stringed instrument. Of David.
verses.text:
Hear my cry, God;
listen to my prayer.

From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart is faint.
Lead me to the rock that is higher than me.

For you are a refuge to me,
a strong tower from the face of the enemy.

Let me sojourn in your tent forever!
I will take refuge in the shelter of your wings. Selah

For you, God, have listened to my vows.
You have given me the inheritance of the fearers of your name.

Days upon days of the king, may you add to his years,
as generation and generation.

May he dwell forever to the face of God.
Appoint covenant faithfulness and truth; may they preserve him.

Thus let me make music to your name forever,
that I may pay my vows day, day.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
verses.text:
Truly toward God my soul is in silence.
From him is my salvation.

He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold.
I will not be greatly shaken.

Until when will you shout at a man?
You will be smashed, all of you,
like a leaning wall, an overthrown fence.

They consult only to cast him down from his elevation.
They delight in a lie;
with his mouth, they bless,
but in their inside, they curse. Selah

Be silent, my soul, toward God alone,
for my hope is from him.

He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold.
I will not be shaken.

In God is my salvation and my glory;
the rock of my strength, my refuge, is in God.

Trust in him in every time, people.
Pour out your heart to his face.
God is a refuge for us. Selah

Surely sons of a human are vapor,
sons of a man are a lie.
To go up on the scales,
they together would be lighter than vapor.

Do not trust in oppression,
and do not hope vainly in robbery.
Wealth, if it increases, do not set the heart.

Once God has spoken, twice I have heard this,
that power is to God.

Also to you, Lord, is covenant faithfulness,
for you, you repay to a man according to his doing.

verses.superscription: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.
verses.text:
God, you are my God. I seek you earnestly.
My soul thirsts for you, my flesh faints for you
in a land of dryness and weary, without water.

Thus in the sanctuary I have gazed at you
to see your power and your glory.

Because your covenant faithfulness is better than life,
my lips will praise you.

Thus I will bless you in my life;
I will lift up my palms in your name.

As with fat and fatness my soul will be full,
and with lips of joyful shouts my mouth will praise you.

When I remember you on my bed,
I meditate on you in the night watches.

For you have been a help to me,
and in the shadow of your wings I shout joyfully.

My soul clings after you;
your right hand upholds me.

But they, they seek my life for devastation;
they will come into the lowest parts of the earth.

They will pour him into the hands of the sword;
they will be a portion of jackals.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.
verses.text:
Hear my voice, God, in my complaint.
Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

Hide me from the council of evildoers,
from the throng of the workers of iniquity,

who have sharpened their tongue like a sword.
They tread their arrow, a bitter word,

to shoot the innocent from secret places;
suddenly they shoot, and they do not fear.

They devise iniquities.
“We have perfected a well-devised device!”
Both the inside of man and the heart are deep.

But God will shoot an arrow;
suddenly their wounds will happen.

And they will make it stumble over them, their tongue.
Everyone seeing them will flee.

And all of mankind will fear,
and they will declare the work of God,
for they will consider his deed.

The righteous will rejoice in Yahweh and take refuge in him,
and all of the upright of heart will celebrate.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David. A song.
verses.text:
Praise is in silence toward you, God, in Zion,
and to you a vow will be paid.

Hearer of prayer,
to you all flesh will come.

Matters of iniquities prevail against me;
our transgressions, you, you cover them.

The happinesses of the one you choose and bring near,
that he may dwell in your courts!
May we be full of the goodness of your house,
the holiness of your temple.

Doing fearsome things, you answer us in righteousness,
God of our salvation,
the confidence of all of the ends of the earth
and the distant seas,

the one establishing mountains by his strength,
being girded with might;

the one stilling the roar of the seas,
the roar of their waves,
and the tumult of the peoples.

And the dwellers of the ends fear at your signs;
you make the goings forth of the morning and the evening shout joyfully.

Watering its furrows,
settling its ridges,
you soften it with showers;
you bless its growth.

You crown the year with your goodness,
and your tracks drip fatness.

The pastures of the wilderness drip,
and the hills gird on rejoicing.

The meadows put on a flock,
and the valleys cover themselves with grain.
They shout joyfully;
indeed, they sing.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; a song; a psalm.
verses.text: Shout to God, all of the earth!

Make music to the glory of his name;
make his praise glorious.

Say to God, “How fearsome are your deeds!
Because of the greatness of your power, your enemies cringe before you.

Come and see the works of God,
fearsome in doing toward the sons of man.

Bless our God, peoples,
and make the sound of his praise heard,

the one putting our soul among the living,
and he does not allow our foot to slip.

For you tested us, God;
you refined us like the refining of silver.

You brought us into a net;
you put pressure on our loins.

I will come into your house with burnt offerings;
I will pay my vows to you,

for which my lips opened
and my mouth spoke when trouble was to me.

Come, listen, and let me recount,
all fearers of God,
what he has done for my soul.

I called to him with my mouth,
and he was exalted from my tongue.

If I had regarded iniquity in my heart,
the Lord would not have heard.

Surely God has heard;
he has attended to the voice of my prayer.

Blessed be God,
who has not turned away my prayer
or his covenant faithfulness from me.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.
verses.text:
May God be gracious to us and bless us;
may he make his face shine on us, Selah

for the knowing of your way on the earth,
your salvation among all of the nations.

May the peoples thank you, God;
may the peoples thank you, all of them.

May the peoples thank you, God;
may the peoples thank you, all of them.

The earth has given its produce;
may God, our God, bless us.

May God bless us,
and may all of the ends of the earth fear him.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David. A song.
verses.text:
Let God arise, let his enemies scatter,
and let the ones hating him flee from his face.

But let the righteous rejoice, let them exult to the face of God,
and let them be glad with rejoicing.

Sing to God, make music to his name,
lift up to the one riding over the plains.
In Yah is his name; yes, exult to his face.

A father of orphans and a judge of widows
is God in the abode of his holiness.

God, when you went out to the face of your people,
when you marched in the wilderness, Selah

A rain of generosities you shook out, God;
your inheritance, when it was wearied, you, you established it.

Your flock dwelt in it;
in your goodness, you prepared for the poor, God.

The Lord utters the word;
the women proclaiming good news are a great army.

Kings of armies flee, they flee,
and the habitation of the house, she divides the spoil.

Though you lie down between the sheepfolds,
the wings of a dove covered with silver
and its feathers, with greenness of gold.

When Shaddai scattered kings in it,
it snowed on Zalmon.

Mount Bashan is a mountain of God;
Mount Bashan is a mountain of peaks.

Why do you look enviously, mountains, peaks,
at the mountain God desired for his dwelling?
Indeed, Yahweh will inhabit it forever.

The chariotry of God is two myriads, thousands of repetition.
The Lord is among them; Sinai is in the holy place.

You have ascended to the height,
you have taken captivity captive,
you have received gifts among men
and even among the ones rebelling,
that Yah God might dwell there.

Blessed be the Lord! Day, day he bears for us,
the God of our salvation. Selah

God is to us a God of salvations,
and to Yahweh the Lord are exits from death.

Surely God will crush the head of his enemies,
the pate of hair of the one walking ahead in his trespasses.

The Lord said, “I will bring back from Bashan,
I will bring back from the depths of the sea,

so that your foot may smash in blood,
the tongue of your dogs, its portion from the enemies.”

They see your processions, God,
the processions of my God, my king, into the holy place.

The singers go ahead; the ones playing stringed instruments, behind,
maidens playing timbrels, in the midst.

Bless God in the assemblies,
Yahweh, from the fountain of Israel.

Your God has commanded your strength.
Be strong, God! You have done this for us.

Because of your temple over Jerusalem,
kings will bring a gift to you.

Rebuke the beast of the reed,
the assembly of the mighty with the calves of the peoples,
humbling himself with pieces of silver.
He scatters the peoples who delight in battles.

Nobles will come from Egypt;
Cush will make its hands run to God.

Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God!
Make music to the Lord, Selah

to the rider on the heavens, of the heavens of antiquity.
Behold, he utters with his voice, a voice of power.

God, you are fearsome from your sanctuary!
The God of Israel, he is giving strength and forces to the people.
Blessed be God!

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on “Lilies”; of David
verses.text:
Save me, God,
for waters have come up to my life.

I have sunk in mire of depth,
and there is no standing.
I have come into depths of waters,
and a flood overflows me.

I am weary in my calling out;
my throat is parched.
My eyes fail
as I am waiting for my God.

The ones hating me gratuitously
are more than the hairs of my head.
The ones destroying me are mighty,
my enemies of falsehood.
What I did not steal,
yet I must restore.

God, you, you know my foolishness,
and my sins are not hidden from you.

May the ones waiting for you not have shame because of me,
Lord Yahweh of Armies.
May the ones seeking you not be humiliated because of me,
God of Israel.

For because of you I have borne reproach;
humiliation has covered my face.

I have become a stranger to my brothers
and a foreigner to the sons of my mother.

For zeal for your house has consumed me,
and the reproaches of the ones reproaching you have fallen on me.

Though I wept in my soul with fasting,
yet it became reproaches to me;

though I made my clothing sackcloth,
yet I became a proverb to them.

The sitters at the gate speak about me,
and the songs of the drinkers of beer.

But I, my prayer is to you, Yahweh.
At a time of favor, God,
in the greatness of your covenant faithfulness,
answer me in the truth of your salvation.

Deliver me from the mire, and let me not sink.
Let me be delivered from the ones hating me
and from the depths of the waters.

Let the flood of waters not overflow me,
and let the deep not swallow me,
and let the pit not close its mouth over me.

Answer me, Yahweh, for your covenant faithfulness is good;
according to the greatness of your compassion, turn to me.

And may you not hide your face from your servant,
for trouble is to me; hurry, answer me.

Draw near to my soul, redeem it;
because of my enemies, ransom me.

You, you know my reproach
and my shame and my humiliation.
All of my adversaries are before you.

Reproach has broken my heart,
and I am sick.
Though I waited for sympathy, yet there was none,
and for comforters, yet I did not find.

But they put gall in my food,
and they made me drink vinegar for my thirst.

Let their table become a snare to their faces
and a trap for their welfare.

Let their eyes darken from seeing,
and make their loins tremble continually.

Pour your indignation on them,
and let the burning of your nose overtake them.

Let their encampment be deserted;
let there not be a dweller in their tents.

For you, whom you have struck, they have persecuted,
and they talk about the pain of your wounded.

Add iniquity to their iniquity,
and let them not come into your righteousness.

Let them be wiped from the book of the living,
and let them not be written with the righteous.

But I am poor and feeling pain;
may your salvation, God, set me on high.

I will praise the name of God with a song,
and I will magnify him with thanksgiving.

And this will be better to Yahweh than an ox,
a bull having horns and having hooves.

The poor will see, they will rejoice;
seekers of God, let your heart live.

For Yahweh is hearing the needy,
and he does not despise his prisoners.

Let the heavens and the earth praise him,
the seas and everything moving in them.

For God will save Zion,
and he will build the cities of Judah,
that they may dwell there and possess it.

And the seed of his servants will inherit it,
and the ones loving his name will dwell in it.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David. To cause to remember.
verses.text:
Hurry, God, to deliver me,
Yahweh, to my help!

Let the ones seeking my life have shame and have confusion;
let the ones delighting in my harm be turned back and disgraced.

Let them turn back on account of their shame,
the ones saying, “Aha! Aha!”

Let all of the seekers of you rejoice and be glad in you,
and let the lovers of your salvation say continually, “God is great!”

In you, Yahweh, I take refuge;
let me not ever have shame.

In your righteousness, deliver me and rescue me;
incline your ear to me and save me.

My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked,
from the palm of the one doing wrong and the one being cruel;

for you are my hope, Lord Yahweh,
my confidence from my youth.

I have become like a wonder to many,
but you are my refuge of strength.

Let my mouth be filled with your praise,
all of the day with your splendor.

May you not cast me away in the time of old age;
may you not forsake me when my strength fails.

For my enemies have spoken against me,
and the ones watching my life have consulted together,

God, may you not be far from me;
my God, hasten to my help.

Let them shame and finish, the adversaries of my life;
let them cover with reproach and disgrace, the ones seeking my harm.

But I, I will hope continually,
and I will add to all of your praise.

My mouth will recount your righteousness,
all of the day, your salvation,
for I do not know the numbers.

I will come in the forces of Lord Yahweh;
I will remember your righteousness, yours alone.

God, you have taught me from my youth,
and to this I declare your wonderful doings.

And also until old age and gray hair,
God, do not forsake me,
until I declare your arm to a generation,
your might to everyone who will come.

You who have made me see many and evil troubles,
may you return, may you revive me,
and may you return, may you bring me up from the depths of the earth.

May you increase my greatness,
and may you turn around, may you comfort me.

My lips will shout joyfully when I make music to you,
and my soul, which you have redeemed.

Also my tongue will meditate on your righteousness all of the day,
for they will shame, for they will confound the ones seeking my harm.

verses.superscription: Of Solomon.
verses.text:
God, give your judgments to the king
and your righteousness to the son of the king.

May he judge your people with righteousness
and your poor with justice.

May the mountains bring peace to the people,
and the hills, in righteousness.

May they fear you with the sun
and to the face of the moon, generation of generations.

May he come down like rain on mown grass,
like showers, a drenching of the earth.

May the righteous flourish in his days,
and abundance of peace until the moon is not.

May he rule from sea to sea
and from the River to the ends of the earth.

May desert-dwellers kneel to his face,
and may his enemies lick the dust.

May the kings of Tarshish and the coastlands return tribute;
may the kings of Sheba and Seba bring near a gift.

And may all kings bow down to him;
may all nations serve him.

For may he deliver the needy crying out
and the poor when no helper is to him.

May he have pity on the weak and the needy,
and may he save the lives of the needy.

May he redeem their life from oppression and from violence,
and may their blood be precious in his eyes.

Blessed be Yahweh God, the God of Israel,
the one doing wonders, he alone.

And blessed be the name of his glory forever,
and let all of the earth be filled with his glory.
Amen and amen.
The prayers of David son of Jesse are finished.

verses.superscription: A psalm of Asaph
verses.text:
Surely God is good to Israel,
to those with a pure heart.

But as for me, my feet almost slipped;
my steps almost were caused to slide out from under me

because I was envious of the arrogant
when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

For they have no ropes until their death,
and their belly is fat.

They are free from the trouble of man,
and with the rest of man they are not afflicted.

Therefore pride is a necklace for them;
a garment of violence covers them.

Their eyes bulge out from fatness;
the imaginations of their heart overflow.

They mock and speak with evil of oppression;
they speak from an elevated place.

They set their mouth in the heavens,
and their tongue goes through the earth.

Therefore his people turn here,
and waters of a full cup are drained by them.

And they say, “How does God know?
And is there knowledge in the Most High?”

Behold, these wicked;
they are always at ease, they increase in wealth.

Surely in vain I have kept my heart clean
and washed my hands in innocence.

For I have been stricken all of the day
and punished every morning.

If I had said, “I will recount such things,”
behold, I would have betrayed the generation of your children.

And when I thought how to understand this,
it was troublesome in my eyes

until I went into the sanctuaries of God,
then I discerned their end.

Surely you set them in slippery places;
you make them fall to destruction.

How they are brought to desolation as in a moment!
They come to an end, they perish by terrors.

Like a dream after one awakes,
Lord, when you rouse yourself, you will despise their image.

When my heart was embittered,
and I was pierced in my kidneys,

I was stupid and I was not knowing;
I was an animal with you.

Yet I am continuously with you;
you hold me by my right hand.

You guide me with your counsel,
and afterward you will take me to glory.

Whom have I in heaven but you?
And besides you there is nothing on the earth I desire.

My flesh and my heart fail,
but God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.

For behold, those who are far from you will perish;
you destroy every one being unfaithful to you.

But for me, the closeness of God for me is good.
I have made the Lord, Yahweh, my refuge
in order to recount all your works.

verses.superscription: A maskil. Of Asaph.
verses.text:
Why, God, have you rejected us forever?
Why does your nose smoke against the flock of your pasture?

Remember your congregation that you acquired in antiquity,
which you redeemed, the tribe of your inheritance,
this Mount Zion on which you have dwelt.

Lift up your feet to the destructions of perpetuity,
to all the enemy has damaged in the holy place.

Your adversaries roared in the midst of your meeting place;
they set up their signs as signs.

It was known like one bringing upward
axes in a thicket of trees.

And now with hatchet and hammers
they have broken down its carvings altogether.

They sent your holy place into fire;
they profaned the dwelling of your name to the ground.

They said in their heart, “Let us oppress them altogether.”
They burned all of the meeting places of God in the land.

Until when, God, will the adversary reproach?
Will the enemy despise your name forever?

Why do you hold back your hand, even your right hand?
From the midst of your bosom finish them!

But God is my king from antiquity,
working salvations in the midst of the earth.

You, you divided the sea by your strength;
you broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.

You, you crushed the heads of Leviathan;
you gave him as food to a people, to the desert-dwellers.

You, you split open spring and wadi;
you, you dry up perpetual rivers.

The day is to you; the night is also to you.
You, you established the light and the sun.

You, you set all of the boundaries of the earth;
summer and winter, you, you formed them.

Remember this: the enemy has reproached Yahweh,
and a foolish people has despised your name.

May you not give the life of your dove to a beast;
may you not forget the life of your poor forever.

Regard the covenant,
for pastures of violence fill the dark places of the land.

May the weak not return ashamed;
may the poor and the needy praise your name.

Arise, God! Plead your case!
Remember your reproach from the fool all of the day.

Do not forget the voice of your adversaries,
the uproar of the ones rising against you, going up continually.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; “May You Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph; a song.

verses.text:
When I take the appointed time;
I, I will judge with equity.

The earth and all its inhabitants are melting;
I, I established its pillars. Selah

I said to the boasters, “Do not boast,”
and to the wicked, “Do not lift up a horn.

Do not lift up your horn to the height,
or speak with an arrogant neck.”

For not from the east or from the west,
and not from the wilderness comes lifting up.

For God is the judge;
this one he brings low, and this one he lifts up.

But I, I will declare to eternity;
I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.

“And all the horns of the wicked I will cut off;
the horns of the righteous will be lifted up.”

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph, a song.
verses.text:
In Judah God is known;
in Israel his name is great.

And his abode is in Salem,
and his dwelling place is in Zion.

There he broke the flames of the bow,
the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Selah

You are shining, majestic,
from the mountains of prey.

At your rebuke, O God of Jacob,
both rider and horse fell deeply asleep.

You, you are to be feared,
and who can stand before your face from the time of your nose?

From heaven you caused judgment to be heard;
the earth feared and was quiet

when God arose to judgment,
to save all the humble of the earth. Selah

For the wrath of man will thank you;
the remainder of wrath you will gird on.

Vow and pay to Yahweh your God;
let all who are around him bring a gift to the Fear.

He cuts off the spirit of princes;
he is to be feared by the kings of the earth.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on Jeduthun; a psalm of Asaph.
verses.text:
My voice is to God, and I cry out;
my voice is to God, and he listens to me.

I remembered God and I groaned;
I meditated, and my spirit grew faint. Selah

You held the lids of my eyes;
I was troubled and I did not speak.

I thought about days from antiquity,
years of long ago.

Will the Lord reject me forever?
And will he not again add to show favor?

Has his covenant faithfulness ceased forever?
Has a promise ended for generation and generation?

Has God forgotten to be gracious?
Or has he shut up his compassions in his nose? Selah

And I said, “This is my wounding:
the changing of the right hand of the Most High.”

I will remember the deeds of Yah;
for I will remember your wonder from antiquity.

And I will ponder on all your deeds,
and on your works I will meditate.

Your way, God, is in holiness;
what god is great like God?

You are the God who does wonders;
you have revealed your strength among the peoples.

You have redeemed your people with your arm,
the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

Your way went through the sea
and your path through many waters,
but your footprints were not discerned.

You led your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

verses.superscription: A maskil of Asaph.
verses.text:
Hear my teaching, my people;
incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

I will open my mouth in a parable;
I will pour out riddles from antiquity.

These are things that we have heard and learned,
things that our fathers have told us.

We will not keep them from their descendants.
We will tell the next generation about the praises of Yahweh,
his strength, and his wonders that he has done.

And he established a testimony in Jacob
and appointed a law in Israel,
which he commanded our fathers
to teach them to their children,

So that the later generation might know, the children yet to be born,
and they will rise up and tell to their children.

And they would place their confidence in God
and not forget the deeds of God
but keep his commandments.

And they would not be like their fathers,
a stubborn generation and a rebellious generation,
which did not cause its heart to be steadfast,
and its spirit was not faithful with God.

The sons of Ephraim being armed with shooters of bows,
they turned back on the day of battle.

They did not keep the covenant of God,
and they refused to walk in his law.

And they forgot his deeds,
and his wonders that he had shown them.

He did wonders before their fathers
in the land of Egypt, in the territory of Zoan.

He divided the sea and led them across it,
and he made the waters to stand like a heap.

And by day he led them with the cloud
and all the night with the light of fire.

He split open the rocks in the wilderness,
and he gave drink abundantly as the deep.

He made streams flow out of the rock
and made the water flow like rivers.

And they added still to sin against him,
to rebel against the Most High in the dry land.

And they tested God in their hearts
by asking for food for their appetite.

And they spoke against God.
They said, “Can God arrange a table in the wilderness?

Behold, he struck the rock
and waters gushed out
and streams overflowed.
Is he able to give bread also?
Or can he provide meat for his people?”

Therefore, Yahweh heard and was furious,
and a fire was kindled against Jacob,
and also his nose went up against Israel,

because they did not believe in God
and did not trust in his salvation.

Yet he commanded the clouds from above
and opened the doors of the sky.

And he rained down manna to eat on them,
and gave to them the grain of heaven.

Man ate the bread of the mighty.
He sent to them provision to their satisfaction.

He caused the east wind to blow in the sky,
and by his power he guided the south wind.

And he rained down meat on them like dust,
and birds of wing as the sands of the sea.

And he caused them to fall in the middle of his camp,
around his dwellings.

And they ate and were very satisfied.
And he brought their craving to them.

They were not separated from their craving,
their food was still in their mouth,

and the nose of God went up in them
and he killed some of their stoutest people,
and he caused the young men of Israel to bow down.

In all this they sinned again,
and did not believe in his wonders.

So he consumed their days in a vapor,
and their years in terror.

When he killed them, then they would seek him,
and they would return and look earnestly for God.

And they would remember that God was their rock
and that God Most High was their redeemer.

And they would deceive him with their mouth
and lie to him with their tongues.

And their hearts were not steadfast with him,
and they were not faithful in his covenant.

Yet he, being merciful, atoned for their iniquity and did not destroy them.
And many times he held back his nose
and did not stir up all his wrath.

And he remembered that they were flesh,
a wind going and it does not return.

How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness!
They grieved him in the desert!

And they returned and they tested God
and grieved the Holy One of Israel.

They did not remember his hand,
the day when he redeemed them from the adversary,

when he set his signs in Egypt
and his wonders in the field of Zoan.

And he turned their rivers to blood
and their streams they could not drink.

He sent a swarm among them, and it devoured them,
and the frog and it destroyed them.

And he gave their produce to the locust
and their labor to the swarming locust.

He slew their vines with hail
and their sycamore trees with frost.

And he gave over their cattle to the hail
and their livestock to the bolts of lightning.

He sent among them the burning of his nose,
fury and indignation and distress,
a group of messengers of calamity.

And he struck every firstborn in Egypt,
the beginning of strength in the tents of Ham.

And he made his people journey like sheep,
and he led them like a flock in the wilderness.

And he guided them in security, and they did not fear,
and the sea covered their enemies.

And he brought them to the border of his holiness,
this mountain that his right hand acquired.

And he drove out nations from before them
and caused them to fall in a portion of inheritance,
and he caused the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.

But they tested and rebelled against God Most High,
and they did not keep his testimonies.

And they turned back and acted treacherously like their fathers;
they turned themselves like a bow of deceit.

And they provoked him to anger with their high places,
and with their carved images they moved him to jealousy.

God heard and was furious,
and he rejected Israel greatly.

And he abandoned the dwelling of Shiloh,
the tent in which he had dwelt among mankind.

And he gave his strength to captivity
and his splendor into the hand of the enemy.

And he delivered his people over to the sword,
and he was furious with his inheritance.

Fire consumed his young men,
and his virgins were not praised in wedding songs.

His priests fell by the sword,
and his widows did not weep.

Then the Lord awoke as one sleeping,
as a mighty man shouting from wine.

And he struck his adversaries backward;
he gave to them a reproach of perpetuity.

And he rejected the tent of Joseph,
and he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.

But he chose the tribe of Judah,
Mount Zion, which he loved.

And he built his sanctuary like the heights,
like the earth he founded it forever.

And he chose David his servant
and took him from the folds of the flock.

From behind the nursing ewes he brought him,
to shepherd Jacob his people
and Israel his inheritance.

And he shepherded them according to the integrity of his heart,
and with the skillfulness of his hands he guided them.

verses.superscription: A psalm. Of Asaph.

verses.text:
They have given the corpse of your servants as food to the bird of the heavens,
the flesh of your faithful to the beast of the earth.

They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem,
and there is no burying.

We have become a reproach to our neighbors,
scorn and derision to the ones around us.

Until when, Yahweh? Will you be angry forever?
Will your jealousy burn like fire?

Pour out your wrath on the nations that have not known you
and on the kingdoms that have not called on your name.

For one has devoured Jacob,
and they have desolated his habitation.

Help us, God of our salvation, on account of the glory of your name, and deliver us
and cover over our sins for the sake of your name.

Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?”
Let the vengeance of the poured-out blood of your servants
be known among the nations to our eyes.

Let the groaning of the prisoner come to your face;
according to the greatness of your arm, preserve the sons of death.

And return to our neighbors sevenfold, into their bosom,
their reproach with which they have reproached you, Lord.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on “Lilies.” A testimony. Of Asaph; a psalm.
verses.text:
Shepherd of Israel, give ear,
the one leading Joseph like a flock.
Sitter on the cherubim, shine forth.

To the face of Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh,
awaken your might and come to us for salvation.

God, restore us,
and make your face shine and let us be saved.

Yahweh, God of armies,
until when will you smolder against the prayer of your people?

You have made them eat bread of tears,
and you have made them drink tears in triple measure.

You have made us strife to our neighbors,
and our enemies mock among themselves.

God of armies, restore us,
and make your face shine and let us be saved.

You pulled up a vine from Egypt;
you drove out nations and planted it.

You cleared to the face of it,
and it rooted its roots and filled the land.

The mountains were covered with its shadow,
and its branches were cedars of God.

It sent out its branches to the sea,
and its shoots to the River.

Why have you broken down its walls,
so that all the ones passing on the way pluck it?

The boar from the forest ravages it,
and the creature of the field grazes on it.

God of armies, return, please.
Look down from heaven and see,
and visit this vine,

even the stock that your right hand planted,
and on the son you strengthened for yourself.

It is burned with fire, it is cut down;
from the rebuke of your face they perish.

Let your hand be on the man of your right hand,
on the son of man you strengthened for yourself.

And we will not turn back from you;
revive us, and we will call on your name.

Yahweh, God of armies, restore us.
Make your face shine, and let us be saved.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on Gittith; of Asaph.
verses.text:
Shout joyfully to God, our strength;
shout out to the God of Jacob.

Raise a song and put forth the tambourine,
the pleasant harp with the lyre.

Blow a shofar at the new moon,
at the full moon for the day of our festival.

For it is a statute for Israel,
a judgment of the God of Jacob.

He set it as a testimony in Joseph
when he went out over the land of Egypt,
where I heard a lip I did not know.

“I removed his shoulder from the burden;
his palms passed from the basket.

Hear, my people, and let me testify against you.
Israel, if you would listen to me!

There shall not be a strange god among you,
and you shall not bow down to a god of foreignness.

I am Yahweh your God,
the one having brought you up from the land of Egypt.
Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.

But my people did not listen to my voice,
and Israel did not submit to me.

So I sent them away in the stubbornness of their heart;
they walked in their counsels.

If only my people were listening to me,
if Israel would walk in my ways!

As a little thing I would subdue their enemies,
and I would turn my hand against their adversaries.

The haters of Yahweh would cringe before him,
and their time would be forever.

And he would feed him with the fat of the wheat,
and I would satisfy you with honey from the rock.”

verses.superscription: A psalm. Of Asaph.
verses.text:
God is standing in the congregation of God;
in the midst of gods he judges:

“Until when will you judge with injustice
and lift up the faces of the wicked? Selah

Judge the poor and the orphan;
vindicate the poor and the destitute.

Rescue the poor and the needy;
deliver them from the hand of the wicked.

I, I said, ‘You are gods
and sons of the Most High, all of you.

But you will die like man,
and like one of the princes, you will fall.’”

Arise, God, judge the earth,
for you, you will inherit among all of the nations.

verses.superscription: A song. A psalm. Of Asaph.
verses.text:
God, may silence not be to you;
do not be still, and do not be quiet, God!

For behold, your enemies roar,
and the ones hating you lift up the head.

They are cunning with counsel against your people,
and they conspire against your treasured ones.

They have said, “Come, and let us destroy them from being a nation,
that the name of Israel may not be remembered anymore.”

For they have conspired against you, heart together;
they have cut a covenant:

the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,

Gebal and Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia with the dwellers of Tyre.

Also Assyria has joined with them;
they are an arm to the sons of Lot. Selah

Do to them as to Midian,
as to Sisera, as to Jabin at the river of Kishon.

They were destroyed at En Dor;
they became dung for the ground.

Make them, their nobles, like Oreb and like Zeeb
and like Zebah and like Zalmunna, all of their princes,

who said, “Let us possess for ourselves
the pastures of God.”

My God, make them like tumbleweed,
like chaff to the face of the wind.

As fire burns a forest,
and as flame kindles mountains,

thus pursue them with your tempest,
and terrify them with your whirlwind.

Fill their faces with shame,
that they may seek your name, Yahweh.

May they have shame and be terrified, eternities of eternity,
and may they have disgrace and may they perish.

And may they know that you, your name is Yahweh,
you alone are the Most High over all of the earth.

verses.superscription: For the chief musician; on Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
verses.text:
How amiable are your dwellings,
Yahweh of Armies!

My soul longs and even faints
for the courts of Yahweh;
my heart and my flesh cry out
to the living God.

Even the sparrow has found a house,
and the swallow, a nest for herself,
where she may lay her young—
your altars, Yahweh of Armies,
my king and my God.

The happinesses of the dwellers of your house!
They praise you continually. Selah

The happinesses of the man, strength to him is in you!
Highways are in their heart.

They go from strength to strength;
each one appears before God in Zion.

Yahweh, God of armies, hear my prayer;
listen, God of Jacob. Selah

See our shield, God,
and regard the face of your anointed.

For a day in your courts is better than a thousand.
I choose to stand at the threshold in the house of my God
rather than dwell in the tents of wickedness.

For Yahweh God is a sun and a shield;
Yahweh gives favor and glory.
He does not withhold good
from the ones walking in blamelessness.

Yahweh of Armies,
the happinesses of the man trusting in you!

verses.superscription: For the chief musician. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
verses.text:
You favored your land, Yahweh;
you restored the captivity of Jacob.

You bore the iniquity of your people;
you covered all of their sin. Selah

You gathered up all of your wrath;
you turned back from the burning of your nose.

Restore us, God of our salvation,
and break up your vexation with us.

Will you be angry with us forever?
Will you prolong your nose to generation and generation?

You, will you not return?
May you revive us, that your people may rejoice in you.

Make us see your covenant faithfulness, Yahweh,
and give your salvation to us.

Surely his salvation is near to his reverent ones,
for glory to dwell in our land.

Covenant faithfulness and truth will meet together;
righteousness and peace will kiss.

Truth will sprout from the earth,
and righteousness will look down from the heavens.

Also, Yahweh will give the good,
and our land will give its produce.

Righteousness walks before him,
and it puts his steps in the way.

verses.superscription: A prayer. Of David.
verses.text:
Incline your ear, Yahweh;
answer me, for I am poor and needy.

Guard my soul, for I am faithful.
You, my God, save your servant,
the one trusting in you.

Favor me, Lord,
for to you I call all of the day.

Gladden the soul of your servant,
for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.

For you, Lord, are good and forgiving
and plentiful of covenant faithfulness to all of the ones calling on you.

Listen to my prayer, Yahweh,
and attend to the voice of my pleas.

In the day of my trouble I call on you,
for you will answer me.

There is none like you among the gods, Lord,
and there is nothing like your works.

All of the nations that you have made
will come and bow down to your face, Lord,
and they will glorify your name.

For you are great and are doing wonderful things;
you are God, you alone.

Teach me your way, Yahweh.
that I may walk in your truth.
Unite my heart to fear your name.

I will thank you, Lord my God, with all of my heart,
and I will glorify your name forever.

For your covenant faithfulness is great toward me,
and you have delivered my soul from lowest Sheol.

God, the arrogant arise against me,
and the congregation of the violent seek my life,
and they do not set you before them.

But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God,
long of nostrils and plentiful of covenant faithfulness and truth.

Work for me a sign for good,
that the ones hating me may see and have shame,
for you, Yahweh, you help me and comfort me.

verses.superscription: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.
verses.text: His foundation is on the mountains of holiness.

Yahweh is loving the gates of Zion
more than all of the dwellings of Jacob.

Glorious things are spoken of you,
city of God. Selah

I will mention Rahab and Babylon
to the ones knowing me;
behold, Philistia and Tyre
with Cush—
“This one was born there.”

And of Zion it will be said,
“Man and man was born in her,
and he, he will establish her,
the Most High.”

Yahweh will recount in the writing of the peoples,
“This one was born there.” Selah

And the singers, like the pipers,
“All of my springs are in you.”

verses.superscription: A song. A psalm. Of the sons of Korah. For the chief musician. On “Weakness of Afflicting.” A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.
verses.text:
Yahweh, God of my salvation,
by day, in the night, I cry out before you.

Let my prayer come to your face;
incline your ear to my cry.

For my soul is full of troubles,
and my life has come near to Sheol.

I am reckoned with the ones going down into the pit;
I have become like a man without strength,

free among the ones having died,
like the slain lying in the grave,
whom you do not remember them anymore,
and they, they are cut off from your hand.

You have set me in the pit of the depths,
in dark places, in deep places.

Your wrath rests heavily on me,
and you overwhelm me with all of your waves. Selah

Will you do a wonder for the ones having died?
Or will the Raphaites arise? Will they thank you? Selah

Will your covenant faithfulness be recounted in the grave,
your faithfulness in Abaddon?

Will your wonder be known in the darkness,
or your righteousness, in the land of forgetfulness?

But I, I cry out to you, Yahweh,
and in the morning my prayer precedes you.

Why, Yahweh, do you reject my soul?
Why do you hide your face from me?

I have been weak and expiring since youth;
I have borne your terrors; I must despair.

Your indignations pass over me;
your terrors destroy me.

They surround me like water all of the day;
they close in upon me together.

You have distanced friend and acquaintance from me;
the ones known to me are darkness.

verses.superscription: A maskil. Of Ethan the Ezrahite.
verses.text:
I will sing the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh forever;
to generation and generation I will make known your faithfulness with my mouth.

For I said, “Covenant faithfulness will be built up forever;
the heavens, you establish your faithfulness in them.”

“I have cut a covenant with my chosen;
I have sworn to David my servant:

‘Until forever I will establish your seed,
and I will build up your throne to generation and generation.’” Selah

And the heavens praise your wonder, Yahweh;
your faithfulness also, in the assembly of the holy ones.

For who in the sky arrays with Yahweh,
compares to Yahweh among the sons of God?

God is greatly dreaded in the council of the holy ones
and feared above all of the ones around him.

Yahweh, God of Armies,
who is like you, mighty Yah?
And your faithfulness is your surroundings.

You are ruling over the surging of the sea;
when its waves rise, you, you still them.

You, you shattered Rahab like a slain one;
with the arm of your strength you scattered your enemies.

To you are the heavens, also to you, the earth;
the world and its fullness, you, you founded them.

The north and the south, you, you created them;
Tabor and Hermon shout joyfully in your name.

To you is an arm with might;
your hand is strong; your right hand is high.

Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne;
covenant faithfulness and truth precede your face.

The happinesses of the people knowing the joyful shout!
Yahweh, they walk in the light of your face.

In your name they rejoice all of the day,
and in your righteousness they rise high;

for you are the splendor of their strength,
and by your favor you raise up our horn.

For our shield is to Yahweh,
and our king, to the Holy One of Israel.

I have found David my servant;
I have anointed him with the oil of my holiness,

with whom my hand will be established;
my arm will also strengthen him.

The enemy will not exact from him,
and a son of wickedness will not oppress him.

And I will crush his adversaries from his face,
and I will strike down the ones hating him.

And my faithfulness and my covenant faithfulness will be with him,
and in my name his horn will be high.

And I will set his hand on the sea
and his right hand on the rivers.

He, he will call to me, ‘You are my Father,
my God and the rock of my salvation.’

And I, I will make him the firstborn,
the highest of the kings of the earth.

I will keep my covenant faithfulness for him forever,
and my covenant will be confirmed to him.

And I will set up his seed forever
and his throne like the days of the heavens.

If his sons forsake my law
and they do not walk in my judgments,

if they profane my statutes
and they do not keep my commandments,

then I will punish their transgression with a rod
and their iniquity with blows.

But my covenant faithfulness I will not break off from him,
and I will not deal falsely in my faithfulness.

I will not profane my covenant,
and I will not change the utterance of my lips

Once I have sworn by my holiness,
‘If I should lie to David!

His seed will be forever,
and his throne, like the sun before me.

It will be established forever like the moon,
yes, the attested witness in the sky.’” Selah

But you, you have rejected and spurned;
you have passed yourself over from your anointed one.

You have voided the covenant of your servant;
you have profaned his crown to the ground.

You have broken down all of his walls;
you have made his fortifications a ruin.

All of the passers of the way plunder him;
he has become a reproach to his neighbors.

You have raised up the right hand of his adversaries;
you have made all of his enemies rejoice.

You have also turned back the edge of his sword,
and you have not made him stand in battle.

You have made his splendor cease,
and you have cast his throne to the ground.

You have shortened the days of his youth;
you have covered him over with shame. Selah

Until when, Yahweh? Will you hide yourself forever?
Will your wrath burn like fire?

Remember me, what life is,
for what emptiness you created all of the sons of man.

What man will live and not see death,
will deliver his soul from the hand of Sheol? Selah

Where are your former covenant faithfulnesses, Lord,
which you swore to David in your faithfulness?

Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants;
my carrying in my bosom all of many peoples

with which your enemies have taunted, Yahweh,
with which they have taunted the footsteps of your anointed.

Blessed be Yahweh forever!
Amen and amen.

verses.superscription: A prayer of Moses, the man of God.
verses.text:
Lord, you have been a habitation to us
in generation and generation.

Before the mountains were born
or you brought forth the earth and the world,
even from forever to forever, you are God.

You cause man to return to dust,
and you say, “Return, sons of man.”

For a thousand years in your eyes
are like the day before when it has passed,
and a watch in the night.

You flood them away—they are sleep;
in the morning, like grass, it passes along.

In the morning it sprouts and passes along;
in the evening it withers and dries up.

For by your nose, we perish,
and by your wrath we are terrified.

You have set our iniquities before you,
our hidden sin in the light of your face.

For all of our days turn in your wrath;
we end our years like a sigh.

The days of our years, in them are 70 years,
or, if by strength, 80 years
but their expanse is trouble and sorrow,
for it passes quickly, and we fly away.

Who knows the power of your nose,
or your wrath according to your fear?

So teach us to number our days
that we might bring in a heart of wisdom.

Return, Yahweh! Until when?
Have compassion on your servants.

Satisfy us in the morning with your covenant faithfulness
and we will rejoice and be glad in all of our days.

Make us glad according to the days you afflicted us
the years we have seen trouble.

May your work be seen by your servants,
and your majesty by their sons.

The one dwelling in the shelter of the Most High
will remain in the shadow of Shaddai.

I will say to Yahweh, “My refuge and my fortress,
my God, I trust in him.”

For he will rescue you from the snare of the trapper,
from the plague of calamities.

He will cover you with his feathers,
and under his wings you will shelter.
His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.

You will not be afraid of the terror of the night,
of the arrow that flies by day,

of the plague that walks in darkness,
of the destruction that wastes at midday.

You will only observe with your eyes
and see the recompense of the wicked.

Because you have made Yahweh, my refuge,
the Most High, your dwelling,

evil will not happen to you,
and a plague will not approach your tent.

For he will command his angels concerning you,
to guard you in all of your ways.

They will lift you up in their hands,
lest you hit your foot against a stone.

You will tread on the lion and the adder;
you will trample the young lion and the serpent.

“Because he clings to me, indeed I will deliver him.
I will protect him because he knows my name.

I will satisfy him with length of days,
and I will show him my salvation.”

verses.superscription: A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day.
verses.text:
It is good to give thanks to Yahweh
and to sing praises to your name, Most High,

to proclaim your covenant faithfulness in the morning
and your truthfulness in the nights,

For you, Yahweh, have made me glad through your deeds.
I will sing for joy because of the deeds of your hands.

How great are your deeds, Yahweh!
Your thoughts are very deep.

A brutish person does not know,
nor does a stupid one understand this:

When the wicked sprout like grass,
and all evildoers thrive,
they will be destroyed for eternity.
But you, Yahweh, are exalted forever.

For behold your enemies, Yahweh!
For behold your enemies—they will perish!
All those who do evil will be scattered.

But you have lifted up my horn like a wild ox;
I am saturated with fresh oil.

My eye has looked on my foes, those rising up against me;
those doing evil my ears have heard.

The righteous one will flourish like the palm tree;
he will grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

They are planted in the house of Yahweh;
they flourish in the courts of our God.

They bear fruit even when they are old;
they are juicy and green,

to proclaim that Yahweh is just,
my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.

Your throne is established from before;
you are from everlasting.

More than the sounds of many waters,
than the mighty breakers of the sea,
Yahweh on high is mighty.

God of vengeance,
Yahweh, God of vengeance,
shine forth!

Rise up, judge of the earth,
return recompense upon the proud.

Until when will the wicked, Yahweh,
until when will the wicked rejoice?

They pour out, they speak, arrogance;
all doers of evil praise themselves.

They crush your people, Yahweh;
they afflict your inheritance.

They kill the widow and the sojourner,
and they murder the fatherless.

They say, “Yah does not see,
the God of Jacob does not perceive.”

Understand, stupid ones among the people!
O fools, when will you have insight?

The one planting the ear, does he not hear?
Or the one forming the eye, does he not observe?

The one instructing nations, does he not rebuke?
Does the one teaching mankind lack knowledge?

Yahweh knows the thoughts of mankind,
that they are vapor.

The joys of the man whom you instruct, Yah,
and from your law you teach him,

to give rest to him from days of evil
until a pit is dug for the wicked.

For Yahweh will not forsake his people
and he will not abandon his inheritance.

For judgment will return to the right;
and all the upright in heart are after it.

Who will rise up for me against the evildoers?
Who will stand up for me against the workers of wickedness?

Unless Yahweh had been a help to me,
shortly my soul would have dwelt in silence.

When I said, “My foot is slipping,”
Your covenant faithfulness, Yahweh, supported me.
When my cares within me are many, your consolations gladden my soul.

Can a throne of destruction be your ally,
one creating injustice by statute?

They conspire together against the life of the righteous
and they condemn innocent blood.

But Yahweh has been to me a high tower,
and my God, the rock of my refuge.

He will return on them their iniquity
and he will destroy them in their wickedness.
Yahweh our God will destroy them.

Come, let us sing to Yahweh;
let us shout to the rock of our salvation!

Let us meet his face with thanksgiving;
with psalms, let us sing joyfully to him.

For Yahweh is a great God
and a great king above all gods,

who in his hand has the depths of the earth;
and the heights of the mountains are to him,

who to him is the sea, and he, he made it,
and his hands formed the dry land.

Come, let us worship and bow down;
let us kneel to the face of Yahweh, our maker:

For he is our God,
and we are the people of his pasture and the flock of his hand.
Today—if only you would listen to his voice!

“Do not harden your heart, as at Meribah,
as on the day of Massah in the wilderness,

where your fathers tested me,
tried me, though they had seen my deeds.

For 40 years I was angry with the generation
and said, ‘They are a people wandering of heart
and they, they have not known my ways.’

Therefore I vowed in my nose,
‘if they enter into my rest.’”

Sing to Yahweh a new song;
sing to Yahweh, all the earth.

Sing to Yahweh, bless his name;
announce his salvation from day to day.

Recount his glory among the nations,
his marvelous deeds among all the peoples.

For Yahweh is great and is to be praised greatly.
He is to be feared above all gods.

For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but Yahweh made the heavens.

Splendor and majesty are to his face.
Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

Ascribe to Yahweh, clans of peoples,
ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.

Give to Yahweh the glory of his name.
Bring an offering and come into his courts.

Bow down to Yahweh in the splendor of holiness;
tremble from his face, all the earth.

Say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns.”
Indeed, the world is established; it cannot be shaken.
He judges the peoples with evenness.

Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice;
let the sea roar and its fullness.

Let the fields rejoice and all that is in them.
Then let all the trees in the forest shout for joy

to the face of Yahweh, for he is coming,
for he is coming to judge the earth.
He will judge the world with righteousness
and the peoples with his faithfulness.

Yahweh reigns; let the earth rejoice;
let the many coastlands be glad.

Clouds and darkness surround him.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.

Fire goes to his face
and burns his adversaries all around.

His lightning lights up the world;
the earth sees and trembles.

The mountains melt like wax from to the face of Yahweh,
from to the face of the Lord of all the earth.

The heavens declare his righteousness,
and all the peoples see his glory.

Let all those serving a carved image have shame,
those boasting in worthless idols—
bow down to him, all you gods!

Zion heard and was glad,
and the daughters of Judah rejoiced
because of your judgments, Yahweh.

For you, Yahweh, are most high above all the earth.
You are exalted far above all gods.

Lovers of Yahweh, hate evil!
The protector of the lives of his faithful,
from the hand of the wicked he snatches them.

Light is sown for the righteous
and for the upright of heart, gladness.

Be glad in Yahweh, you righteous;
and give thanks to the remembrance of his holiness!

verses.superscription: A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh has made known his salvation;
to the eyes of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.

He remembers his covenant loyalty and his faithfulness to the house of Israel;
all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.

Shout to Yahweh, all the earth;
burst into song, sing for joy, and make music!

Make music to Yahweh with the harp,
with the harp and the voice of a song.

With trumpets and the sound of the shofar,
shout to the face of the King, Yahweh!

Let the sea roar and its fulness,
the world and the dwellers in it!

Let the rivers clap palm;
let the mountains rejoice together

Yahweh reigns—let the peoples tremble—
sitting above the cherubim; let the earth quake!

Yahweh in Zion is great,
and he is high above all the peoples.

Let them praise your great and fearsome name;
holy is he.

Exalt Yahweh our God
and worship at the stool for his feet.
Holy is he.

Moses and Aaron were among his priests,
and Samuel was among those calling his name.
They called to Yahweh, and he, he answered them.

In the pillar of cloud he spoke to them.
They kept his testimonies
and the statutes he gave to them.

Yahweh our God, you, you answered them.
A forgiving God you were to them,
but avenging concerning their deeds.

Exalt Yahweh our God,
and worship at the hill of his holiness,
for Yahweh our God is holy.

verses.superscription: A psalm of thanksgiving.
verses.text: Shout to Yahweh, all the earth.

Serve Yahweh with gladness;
come to his face with rejoicing.

Enter his gates with thanksgiving
and his courts with praise.
Give thanks to him; bless his name.

For Yahweh is good; his covenant faithfulness is to eternity
and his truthfulness until generation and generation.

verses.superscription: A psalm of David
verses.text:
I shall sing of covenant faithfulness and justice;
to you, Yahweh, I shall sing praises.

I shall study the blameless way.
When will you come to me?
I will walk in the integrity of my heart within my house.

A perverse heart will turn away from me;
I will not know evil.

The one slandering his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy.
The one lofty of eyes and the one wide of heart, him I cannot.

My eyes are on the faithful ones of the land to sit with me;
The one walking in the way of integrity, he may serve me.

A doer of deceit will not remain within my house;
a speaker of lies will not be established before my eyes.

In the mornings I will destroy all the wicked of the land,
to cut off all workers of evil from the city of Yahweh.

verses.superscription: A prayer of the lowly when he is faint and pours out his meditation to the face of Yahweh.
verses.text:
Hear my prayer, Yahweh;
let my cry come unto you.

Do not hide your face from me on the day it distresses me.
Incline your ear to me.
On the day I call out, hurry, answer me.

For my days expire like smoke,
and my bones are charred like a fireplace.

My heart is struck like grass and withered,
for I have forgotten to eat my bread.

From the voice of my groaning,
my bone clings to my flesh.

I am like an owl of the wilderness;
I have become like a screech owl in the ruins.

I am alert,
and I have become like a bird alone on a roof.

My enemies taunt me all the day;
those mocking me swear by me.

As ashes as bread I eat,
and I mix my drink with weeping

from the face of your fury and rage,
for you have lifted me up and thrown me.

My days are like a lengthening shadow,
and I, like grass, have withered.

But you, Yahweh, sit forever,
and your remembrance is to generation and generation.

For your servants cherish her stones
and favor her dust.

The nations will fear the name of Yahweh,
and all the kings of the earth, your glory.

For Yahweh builds Zion;
he appears in his glory.

He turns to the prayer of the destitute
and he does not despise their prayer.

This will be written for a future generation,
and a people being created will praise Yah;

that he looked down from the height of his holiness;
Yahweh from heaven regarded the earth,

to hear the groaning of the prisoner,
to release the sons of execution.

To recount the name of Yahweh in Zion
and his praise in Jerusalem

when peoples and kingdoms gather together
to serve Yahweh.

He has broken my strength on the road.
He has shortened my days.

I said, “My God, do not take me away in the middle of my days;
your years are a generation of generations.

Formerly you set the earth,
and the heavens are the work of your hands.

But you are he,
and your years will not end.

The sons of your servants will abide,
and their seed will be established to your face.”

verses.superscription: Of David
verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
And all of my inward parts, the name of his holiness.

Bless Yahweh, my soul!
And do not forget all of his benefits.

The one pardoning all your sins;
the one healing all your diseases.

The one redeeming your life from the pit;
the one crowning you with covenant faithfulness and mercy.

The one satisfying your ornaments with good;
your youth renews itself like the eagle.
Yahweh, doing righteousness and justice for all those being oppressed.

He made known his ways to Moses,
his deeds to the children of Israel.

Yahweh is merciful and gracious,
long of nostrils and abundant in covenant faithfulness.

He will not contend to the end,
and he will not maintain forever.

He does not deal with us according to our sins,
and he does not treat us according to our iniquities.

For as the heavens are high above the earth,
his covenant faithfulness is strong toward those fearing him.

As far as the sunrise is from the sunset,
he has removed our transgressions from us.

As a father has compassion on his children,
Yahweh has compassion on those fearing him.

For he, he knows our form;
remembering that we are dust.

A man, his days are like grass;
like a flower of the field, thus he flourishes.

For the wind passes over it, and it is no more,
and its place does not acknowledge it again.

But the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh is from everlasting to everlasting on those fearing him,
and his righteousness is to the children of children,

to the ones keeping his covenant,
and to the ones remembering his precepts, to do them.

Yahweh has established his throne in the heavens,
and his kingdom rules over all.

Bless Yahweh, his angels,
warriors of strength, doers of his word,
listening to the voice of his word!

Bless Yahweh, all his hosts,
ministering to him, doing his pleasure!

Bless Yahweh, all his works,
in all the places of his reign!
Bless Yahweh, my soul!

wrapping light as the garment;
spreading out the heavens as the tent curtain;

making the winds his messengers,
flaming fire, his servants.

He set the earth upon its foundations;
it will not be moved forever and ever.

You covered it with the deep like a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.

From your rebuke they fled;
from your voice of thunder they hurried away.

They ascended the mountains; they descended the valleys,
to the place that you had appointed for them.

You set a boundary they cannot pass;
they will not return to cover the earth.

The one sending springs into the wadis—
between the mountains they flow.

They give drink to all his animals of the field;
the wild donkeys break their thirst.

Alongside them the birds of the heavens dwell;
from between the branches they give voice.

The one watering the mountains from his upper chambers—
from the fruit of your works the earth is satisfied.

The one making grass grow for the cattle
and plants for the work of man
to bring forth bread from the earth.

And wine—he gladdens the heart of man,
to make the face shine from oil,
and bread—he sustains the heart of man.

The trees of Yahweh are satisfied—
the cedars of Lebanon which he planted,

where birds make their nests there,
the stork, the cypress tree her home,

the high mountains for the wild goats,
the cliffs, a refuge for the hyraxes.

He made the moon for appointed times;
the sun knows its setting.

You set darkness and it is night;
in it all of his creatures of the forest crawl—

the young lions roaring for prey
and seeking their food from God.

The sun rises, they retreat,
and lie down in their dens.

Man goes out to his work
and to his labor until evening.

There is the sea, great and broad of hands;
creeping things are there,
and there is no number,
living things, small with great.

Ships travel there;
Leviathan, which you formed to play in it.

All of them look to you to give
their food at its time.

You give to them; they gather it;
you open your hand; they are satisfied with good.

You send out your breath; they are created,
and you renew the face of the land.

May the glory of Yahweh be forever;
may Yahweh rejoice in his creation!

The one looking at the earth, and it shakes—
he touches the mountains, and they smoke.

I shall sing to Yahweh in my life;
I shall sing praise to my God during my existence.

May my meditation be sweet to him;
I, I will rejoice in Yahweh.

May sinners cease from the earth,
and the wicked be no more.
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
Hallelu Yah!

Give thanks to Yahweh, call on his name;
make known his deeds among the peoples!

Sing to him, make music to him;
exclaim about all of his marvelous deeds!

Boast in the name of his holiness;
let the heart of the seekers of Yahweh rejoice.

Seek Yahweh and his strength;
search for his face continually.

Recall the marvelous things that he has done,
his miracles and the decrees from his mouth,

seed of Abraham his servant,
sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.

He is Yahweh, our God.
His decrees are in all the earth.

He remembers his covenant forever,
the word he commanded for a thousand generations,

that he cut with Abraham
and his oath to Isaac.

He confirmed it to Jacob as a statute;
to Israel, an everlasting covenant,

saying, “I will give to you the land of Canaan
as the portion of your inheritance,”

when they were few in number,
very few, and strangers in it.

They wandered from nation to nation,
from a kingdom to other people.

He did not allow anyone to oppress them;
he rebuked kings because of them.

“Do not touch my anointed ones,
and do not harm my prophets.”

He called for a famine on the land;
he broke all of the staff of bread.

He sent a man ahead of them;
Joseph was sold as a servant.

They oppressed his feet in a shackle;
his neck went into the iron,

until the time of his word coming to pass.
The speaking of Yahweh refined him.

The king sent and released him;
the one ruling the people, and liberated him.

He appointed him lord of his house
and ruler over all of his possessions

to bind his princes according to his soul
and he taught his elders wisdom.

Then Israel came into Egypt,
and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.

He made his people very fruitful,
and he made him stronger than his enemies.

He turned their hearts to hate his people,
to plot against his servants.

He sent Moses, his servant,
Aaron, whom he had chosen him.

They performed among them the matters of his signs,
and his wonders in the land of Ham.

He sent darkness and made it dark,
and they did not rebel against his words.

He turned their water into blood
and killed their fish.

Their land swarmed with frogs—
in the rooms of their kings!

He spoke, and flies came;
gnats in all their territory.

He made their rain hail,
fire of flames on their land.

He struck their vines and their figs;
he shattered the trees of their territory.

He spoke, and the locust came,
and the young locust, and there was no number.

And they ate all of the vegetation in their land;
and they ate the fruit of their ground.

Then he struck every firstborn in their land,
the first of all their strength.

He brought them out with silver and gold;
and there was no stumbling among his tribes.

Egypt was glad when they departed,
for the dread of them had fallen upon them.

He spread a cloud for a covering
and fire to light up the night.

He asked, and he brought quail
and satisfied them with bread from heaven.

He split the rock and waters gushed out;
they went forth in the desert a river.

For he remembered the word of his holiness
with Abraham his servant.

He led his people out with joy,
his chosen with shouts of triumph.

Then he gave to them the lands of the nations,
and they took possession of the toil of the peoples

so that they might keep his statutes
and comply with his laws.
Hallelu Yah!

Hallelu Yah!
Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good,
for his covenant faithfulness is to forever.

Who can utter the mighty acts of Yahweh,
proclaim all of his praise?

The happinesses of the guardians of justice,
the doers of righteousness at all times!

Remember me, Yahweh, in the favor of your people;
visit me in your salvation,

to look on the good of your chosen,
to rejoice in the gladness of your nation,
to boast with your inheritance.

We have sinned like our fathers;
we have done wrong; we have done evil.

But he saved them on account of his name,
to make known his power.

He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up.
Then he led them through the depths, as through a desert.

So he saved them from the hand of the hater,
and he rescued them from the hand of the enemy.

Then the waters covered their adversaries;
one of them was not left.

Then they believed his words;
they sang his praise.

But they hurried, they forgot his deeds;
they did not wait for his instructions.

And they craved a craving in the wilderness,
and they tested God in the wasteland.

So he gave to them their request,
but he sent a wasting disease upon their lives.

And they became envious of Moses in the camp,
of Aaron, the holy one of Yahweh.

The earth opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered over the congregation of Abiram.

Fire blazed up in their congregation;
a flame burned up the wicked.

They made a calf at Horeb
and worshiped a cast image.

Thus they traded their Glory
for the likeness of a bull eating grass.

They forgot God their Savior,
the doer of great deeds in Egypt:

wonders in the land of Ham,
awesome acts at the Sea of Reeds.

So he said to annihilate them—
had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach to his face,
to turn away his heat from destroying.

Then they despised the delightful land;
they did not believe his word,

but grumbled in their tents;
they did not listen to the voice of Yahweh.

Then he raised his hand to them
to make them fall in the desert,

and to make their seed fall among the nations,
and to scatter them among the lands.

They joined themselves to the Baal of Peor
and ate the sacrifices of the dead.

And they angered with their actions,
and a plague broke out among them.

Then Phinehas stood and intervened,
and the plague was restrained.

It was counted to him as righteousness
to generation and generation until forever.

And they angered at the waters of Meribah,
and it was bad for Moses on account of them.

For they rebelled against his spirit,
and he spoke rashly with his lips.

They did not destroy the peoples,
which Yahweh had said to them,

but they mingled with the nations
and learned their ways

and served their idols,
and they became a snare to them.
And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.

And they shed innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and their daughters,
whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan,
and the land was desecrated by bloodshed.

And they became unclean by their deeds;
and they prostituted themselves by their actions.

So Yahweh’s nose burned with his people,
and he despised his inheritance.

And he gave them into the hand of the nations,
and the haters of them ruled over them.

And their enemies oppressed them,
and they were humbled under their hand.

Many times he rescued them,
but they, they were rebellious in their counsel
and sank in their sin.

Yet he saw in the narrow to them,
when he was hearing their cry.

And he remembered his covenant with them
and relented because of the abundance of his covenant faithfulness.
He gave them for compassion to the face of all of their captors.

Save us, Yahweh, our God!
Gather us from the nations
to give thanks to the name of your holiness,
to glory in your praises.

May Yahweh, the God of Israel, be blessed
from everlasting and to everlasting,
and all the people say, “Amen.
Hallelu Yah!”

Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good,
for his covenant faithfulness is to forever.

Let the redeemed of Yahweh say it,
who he rescued them from the hand of the opponent.

They wandered in the desert with wilderness for a road;
a city for a home they did not find.

Hungry and thirsty,
their soul fainted within them.

Then they called out to Yahweh in the distressing to them;
he rescued them from their distresses.

He led them by a direct path
to go to a city of dwelling.

May they thank Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
and his amazing deeds for the sons of man!

For he satisfies the thirsty soul,
and the hungry soul he fills with good.

Sitting in darkness and gloom,
prisoners of affliction and iron

because they had rebelled against the words of God
and despised the counsel of the Most High,

he humbled their hearts through hardship;
they stumbled and there was no helper.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in the distressing to them;
he saved them from their distresses.

He brought them out of darkness and gloom
and broke apart their bonds.

May they thank Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
and his amazing deeds for the sons of man!

For he has broken the gates of bronze
and cut through the bars of iron.

Foolish from their rebellious way
and afflicted from their sins,

their soul detested all food,
and they touched the gates of death.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in the distressing to them;
he saved them from their distresses.

He sent his word and healed them,
and he delivered them from their destruction.

May they thank Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
and his amazing deeds for the sons of man!

May they sacrifice sacrifices of thanksgiving
and recount his deeds with a shout!

Going down to the sea in ships,
doing business on abundant waters,

they, they saw the deeds of Yahweh
and his wonders in the deep.

Then he spoke and aroused the wind of a hurricane
and raised up his waves.

They went up to the sky; they went down to the depths.
Their souls melted in the disaster.

They swayed and staggered as intoxicated
and all their wisdom became confounded.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in the distressing to them
and he rescued them from their distresses.

He raised the storm to calmness
and he quieted the waves.

Then they rejoiced because they subsided,
and he guided them to the harbor of their desire.

May they thank Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
and his amazing deeds for the sons of man!

May they exalt him in the assembly of the people
and praise him at the seat of the elders.

He turns rivers into a desert
and springs of water into thirsty land,

fruitful ground into salt land,
from the wickedness of the dwellers in it.

He turns the wilderness into a pool of water
and dry land into springs of water.

He settles the hungry there,
and they build a city of dwelling.

Then they sow fields and plant vineyards,
and they produce the fruit of the harvest.

He blesses them and they become very many
and their cattle do not become few.

Then they become few and become low
from distress of evil and sorrow.

He pours contempt on the leaders
and causes them to wander in an empty place of no road.

But he raises up the needy from affliction
and establishes families like a flock.

The upright see and rejoice,
and all wickedness shuts its mouth.

Who is wise? Then may he keep these things
and may they ponder the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh.

verses.superscription: A song; a psalm of David.
verses.text:
My heart is made steadfast, God;
I will sing and I will make music, indeed, with my glory!

Awaken, lyre and harp;
I will awaken the dawn.

I will thank you, Yahweh, among the peoples;
I will make music to you among the nations.

For your covenant faithfulness is great from above the heavens,
and your trustworthiness, above the clouds.

Be exalted, God, above the heavens,
and your glory, over all the earth.

So that your beloved ones may be rescued,
save with your right hand and answer me.

God has spoken in his holiness: “I shall rejoice;
I shall divide Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

To me is Gilead; to me is Manasseh,
and Ephraim is the protection of my head,
Judah, my scepter.

Who will bring me into the strong city?
Who will lead me to Edom?

God, have you not rejected us?
And you do not go out with our army, God.

Give to us help against the enemy,
and futility is the deliverance of man.

With God we will accomplish valor;
and he, he will trample our adversaries.

verses.superscription: To the chief musician: a psalm of David.
verses.text: God of my praise, do not be silent!

For a wicked mouth and a mouth of deceit open against me;
